{
  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Conduct separate one-way ANOVAs for each continuous response variable (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) with Stim Paradigm as the 5-level categorical factor",
    "For Success (binary outcome), use logistic regression or chi-square test of independence rather than ANOVA",
    "Given severe imbalance in group sizes (Combined n=48846 vs Sham n=3505), use Type III sums of squares and verify homogeneity of variance with Levene's test",
    "Consider Welch's ANOVA or robust alternatives if variance heterogeneity is detected due to large sample size disparities"
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "For continuous variables showing significant ANOVA effects, perform pairwise comparisons using Tukey's HSD if variances are homogeneous",
    "If Welch's ANOVA is required, use Games-Howell post-hoc test which does not assume equal variances",
    "For Success (binary), use pairwise chi-square tests with Bonferroni correction or logistic regression with planned contrasts",
    "Focus comparisons on Combined vs single-modality conditions (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) and all conditions vs Sham baseline",
    "Report effect sizes (eta-squared for ANOVA, Cramer's V or odds ratios for Success)"
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Bonferroni correction across the 5 response variables (familywise alpha = 0.05/5 = 0.01 per variable), with additional Bonferroni correction for the 10 pairwise comparisons per variable (adjusted alpha = 0.001 per comparison) or use False Discovery Rate (FDR) control via Benjamini-Hochberg procedure given the large number of tests",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Multinomial logistic regression is explicitly recommended over ordinary linear regression because Stim Paradigm is a 5-level categorical response with no natural ordering. The model would predict stimulation paradigm membership from the five performance variables (Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD). Alternative: Random Forest or Gradient Boosting classifier given the large sample size (n=76655) and potential nonlinear relationships. If ordinality can be assumed (e.g., Sham < single-modality < Combined), an ordinal logistic regression could be tested, but this requires theoretical justification. Linear discriminant analysis is not recommended due to likely violation of multivariate normality and homogeneity of covariance matrices across the highly imbalanced groups.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Check for outliers in Path Efficiency (max=29.82, mean=0.47) and Time-to-Target (max=201.39, mean=2.81) which suggest extreme right skew",
    "Verify homogeneity of variance with Levene's test; expect violation due to large group size differences and distributional extremes",
    "Assess multivariate normality for discriminant analysis or MANOVA if attempted; likely violated given bounded outcomes (Success binary, AD bounded 0-1)",
    "Check for multicollinearity among predictors in multinomial logistic regression; Path Efficiency and Time-to-Target may be highly correlated",
    "Verify independence of observations within mice; 8 mice with repeated measures suggests need for mixed-effects models or mouse-level clustering"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined stimulation likely shows superior performance (lower Time-to-Target, higher Success, higher Path Efficiency, lower AD) compared to single-modality conditions based on prior multisensory integration literature",
    "ICMS Only may outperform visual-only conditions given direct cortical activation, though this depends on task design",
    "Sham condition expected to show poorest performance (lowest Success, highest Time-to-Target, highest AD)",
    "Dim Visual Only vs Bright Visual Only comparison may reveal luminance-dependent performance differences",
    "Large effect sizes expected for Combined vs Sham; smaller, potentially nonsignificant differences among single-modality conditions after multiple comparison correction",
    "Success rates near 73% overall suggest ceiling effects possible in some conditions"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe group imbalance (Combined: 63.7% of data, Sham: 4.6%) reduces power for Sham comparisons and inflates Type I error risk for Combined-dominated effects",
    "Extreme outliers in Path Efficiency (max 29.82 vs mean 0.47) and Time-to-Target suggest data quality issues or rare event types that may require winsorization or separate analysis",
    "Mouse-level clustering (8 mice, 7,233-10,986 trials each) violates independence assumption; mouse identity is a confound unaddressed in current design",
    "Binary Success outcome with 73% success rate may limit discriminability among conditions",
    "No information on trial order, learning effects, or session structure precludes longitudinal analysis",
    "Summary-only data view prevents trajectory-level analysis that might explain Path Efficiency outliers"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a multinomial logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as response and all five performance variables as predictors, including Mouse as a random effect (mixed-effects multinomial model) or cluster-robust standard errors to account for non-independence. Prior to this, conduct exploratory data analysis with violin plots and compute correlation matrix among predictors. Consider winsorizing Path Efficiency and Time-to-Target at 99th percentile to reduce outlier influence. If computational resources permit, cross-validate the predictive model with stratified sampling to preserve rare classes (Sham, Bright Visual Only)."
}
